title: Oncall handoff notes - Jordan Lee
content:
Shift: 2026-03-03 18:00 - 2026-03-04 02:00 UTC
Owner: Jordan Lee (oncall)
Summary: Quiet shift overall. Saw a spike in 503s around 20:15 UTC linked to a degraded nginx node in prod-west; auto-failover kicked in but some requests retried and caused short tail latency bump (~3m). Open transients: API rate limiter throttle rule SRE-412 still flapping for heavy batching jobs.

Incidents / Alerts handled:
- 20:12 UTC - Alert: prod-west nginx 503 rate increase (pager)
  - Triage: Confirmed multiple 503s from a single host (10.4.21.7).
  - Action: Drained host via k8s node cordon + pod evict, upstream LB marked unhealthy, traffic shifted.
  - Outcome: Error rate back to baseline by 20:16 UTC. No rollback needed.
  - Notes: Host had high CPU and many keepalive connections from a long-lived batching job. Need to follow up with infra to check kernel tcp_keepalive settings.

- 21:40 UTC - Alert: embedding-workers pod OOM (non-pager)
  - Triage: Reproduced locally with embedding workload that spikes mem to ~28GB (node has 32GB). Pod restarted twice.
  - Action: Scaled deployment to 5 -> 7 replicas temporarily. Filed GH issue to add liveness probe and heap limits.
  - Linked artifact: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/issues/456

Temporary runbook additions (draft - needs review):
- When nginx host shows >50 5xx/min but autoscaler not triggered:
  1) Check host CPU/memory (kubectl top node) and connection counts (ss -s).
  2) If host >85% CPU or abnormal conn counts, cordon & drain: kubectl cordon <node>; kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
  3) If upstream LB still routing, mark unhealthy in LB console (prod-west) and escalate to infra on Slack (#infra-alerts).
  4) After drain, verify ingress 2xx rate back to baseline for 5m before uncordoning.
  - TODO: Add exact LB console path and perms required (ticket to infra).

- Embedding worker OOMs:
  1) Temporarily increase replica count and add node taint if capacity allows.
  2) Restarting single pod can be done with kubectl rollout restart deployment/embedding-workers -n prod
  3) Check memory RSS with pmap/top; if memory leak suspected, capture heap/profile and attach to GH issue.
  - Note: Add liveness/readiness checks to prevent noisy restarts.

Outstanding follow-ups (action items):
- Infra: Investigate tcp_keepalive and long-lived connection behavior on prod-west hosts (assigned to Samir). Linked ticket: JIRA-SRE-412.
- Infra: Add LB console path and permission notes to runbook (me -> create ticket).
- Embedding team: Add heap dump capture step in embedding runbook and set resource limits (Aya to follow up).
- Me: Draft PR to add liveness probe for embedding-workers (in progress, see PR #211).

Notes to self / reminders:
- Pager quiet windows: 22:00-23:30 had low alert volume; good time to work on runbook PR.
- Remember to update the oncall checklist with the exact k8s cordon/drain flags we prefer (avoid --force unless escalated).
- If a host is OOMing frequently, pause scheduler on that node to avoid creating too many evictions.

Quick commands (for quick copy):
- kubectl cordon <node>
- kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60
- kubectl rollout restart deployment/embedding-workers -n prod
- kubectl logs deployment/embedding-workers -n prod --since=2h | grep -i oom

Unresolved questions:
- Why did the long-lived batching job create so many keepalive connections? Was there a config drift? Need application owner to confirm.
- Do we have an automated detection rule for "too many keepalive connections from single client IP"? If not, propose one.

Confluence links / docs to update:
- confluence:Oncall-Runbooks (add nginx drain steps + LB path)
- confluence:Embedding-Runbook (add heap dump + resource limits)

End of shift handoff for next oncall (Samir Ali)
- TL;DR: main thing is follow-up on prod-west host behavior + embedding worker OOMs. No ongoing pager-level incidents.
- Ping me on Slack if you need commands or context (I will be online 02:00-03:00 UTC for a quick follow-up window).

Draft status: This is a rough handoff note + temporary runbook entries. Needs to be converted to formal runbook pages and PRs raised for embedding liveness probe and the LB/runbook additions.

-- Jordan
